mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) as of the most recent month is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to reduced discount rates for equity valuation, with the relationship being linear and negative (i.e., lower rates predict higher returns).
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals an economic slowdown that triggers negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns due to heightened recession fears and reduced corporate profit expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) and elevated policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%) signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.0 AND FEDFUNDS > 2.0, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong housing market activity (HOUST > 1000), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward 60-day returns as increased construction and consumer spending boost economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST > 1000, or the Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) as of the most recent month is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns, reflecting robust economic output and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between INDPRO and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly retail sales figure (RSAFS) below 480,000 million dollars signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns as investors anticipate reduced corporate revenues.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS < 480000, or the Rank IC for RSAFS as a predictor of 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of weak job growth (PAYEMS < 130,000 thousand) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to reduced consumer spending and corporate profit pressures.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS < 130000 AND UNRATE > 5.0, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward 60-day returns as higher interest rates reduce corporate leverage and consumer spending, leading to lower equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.0, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 60-day returns in the tightening regime is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
